title: Customer Priority Lattice and Provisional Pin Onboarding Workflow
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement a repeatable workflow that converts customer model requests into prioritized onboarding lanes using a weight-based lattice, enables short-lived provisional 'pins' for urgent enterprise needs, and automates shadow-eval gating and rollback criteria. The workflow should balance SLA-driven priorities with catalog stability and auditability for regulated customers.
background: Enterprise customers frequently request immediate version pins or rapid onboarding for customized model variants. Current ad-hoc triage causes either risky long-lived pins or delayed responses that harm retention. We need a formalized lattice that encodes revenue, SLA tier, compliance needs, and feature-risk to create predictable provisional pathways and automatic safety gates.
goals: 1) Create a transparent scoring lattice that maps request signals to onboarding lanes. 2) Introduce provisional pins with TTL and automated shadow-eval requirements. 3) Provide a documented playbook for PM/SEs to approve fast-paths and for Eng to implement safe rollbacks. 4) Surface audit logs for compliance reviews.
scope: - Design priority scoring rules and thresholds. - Define provisional pin lifecycle (create, monitor, extend/expire, convert to permanent). - Specify shadow-eval metrics and pass/fail thresholds. - Implement metadata fields in catalog for provisional pins and audit trail. - Produce PM-facing runbook and SE template for customer conversations.
out_of_scope: - Building full automatic canary deployments for model variants. - Billing and contract amendments for reserved capacity. - Deep changes to runtime kernel selection; only catalog metadata and routing rules.
proposed_solution: 1) Priority Lattice: a weighted score combining signals: revenue tier (40%), SLA/latency sensitivity (20%), regulatory requirement (20%), feature novelty risk (20%). Score bands map to lanes: Fast-Provisional, Standard-Onboard, Deferred-Eval. 2) Provisional Pin: TTL default 14 days, requires immediate shadow-eval job (30k samples or customer-supplied eval harness) with metrics: hallucination rate, latency delta, regression score. 3) Automation: catalog API accepts provisional_pin=true, ttl_days=14, linked_eval_id; background worker schedules shadow eval and posts results to the ticket and audit log. 4) Rollback/extension rules: Auto-expire unless extend approved; auto-revert traffic routing if shadow-eval fails critical thresholds; manual override requires PM+Eng approval. 5) Observability: dashboard tile for provisional pins with health/status and recent evals.
rollout_plan: 1) Draft lattice scoring doc and review with Sales/CS (2 weeks). 2) Implement catalog metadata and provisional_pin flag + TTL (Eng sprint). 3) Add shadow-eval runner integration and alerting (Eng). 4) Pilot with two enterprise customers for 30-day window. 5) Iterate thresholds and publish playbook + SE template. 6) General availability behind feature-flag.
acceptance_criteria: Priority lattice doc reviewed and approved by Sales, CS, Legal, and SRE.
Catalog supports provisional_pin, ttl_days, sponsor, and linked_eval_id metadata fields.
Shadow-eval automation runs on creation and writes results to audit log and ticket.
Dashboard shows provisional pin status and primary metrics (regression, latency, hallucination).
Pilot completed with two customers and at least one authoritative extension or automated expiry observed.
Playbook published with decision checklist and escalation contacts.
open_questions: What is the minimum sample size and accepted eval sources for shadow-eval (internal vs customer-supplied)?
Should provisional pins be billable differently or be restricted to reserved capacity customers?
What exact thresholds constitute a 'critical' fail that triggers auto-revert?
How do we represent provisional pin state in public API vs console to avoid accidental programmatic dependence?
